outcome: mode of delivery (cesarean section vs. natural delivery)
cohort: The study included 2,085 pregnant women with twin pregnancies who delivered at the First Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing Medical University between June 2006 and October 2019.
finding: Age, history of uterine surgery, and preeclampsia were identified as important factors affecting the mode of delivery in twin pregnancies.
mod_finding: The study found that older age, primiparity, history of uterine surgery, preeclampsia, and higher rates of preterm birth and postpartum hemorrhage were associated with cesarean section in twin pregnancies, while lower rates of DCDA twins were observed in the cesarean section group.
